chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Khazzaz, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from Ja'far, from his father, from Ali (peace be upon him)
That he disliked the use of snuff (snufling) for the fasting person.

key_terms.السُّعُوطَ: Snuff; powdered herbs or spices inhaled into the nose
key_terms.كَرِهَ: He disliked (indicating كراهة, a status between permissibility and prohibition)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on using snuff while fasting in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) expressed dislike (karahah) for the use of snuff (su'oot) by those fasting, a ruling that highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on preserving the spiritual purity of the fast from unnecessary sensory distractions. This narration, found in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, contributes to the jurisprudential discussion on whether actions that enter the body through the nose invalidate the fast or merely constitute a recommended precaution (mustahabb) to avoid.
